prs.title: Strengthen LFD certificates and pursue five validation follow-ups
prs.body_excerpt:
The lift review found two reproducible boundary defects. This PR fixes both and records the results of all five requested local validation tracks. It stays draft because the full depth-14 certificate, split degree-8 result and depth-18 breakpoint remain open.

## Fixes

- Route the inner row reduction through the bounded exact product. At p=16777213, a 64-by-65 counterexample previously gave 16777148 instead of 16777149. Cap requested product chunks at the safe accumulation length.
- Handle an empty next-degree monomial layer at D=2k. The previous code raised IndexError on k=2, D=4, p=17; both proper and unit boundary cases now pass.
- Neither defect reaches the archived depth-14 cases: their primes are below the affected accumulation bound and D=6<2k.
- Correct the paper README's obsolete Lean audit checklist.

prs.title: GPU path for split-presentation closures with m >= 4 summands
prs.body_excerpt:
## Summary

Tracking PR (draft), opened as the first step of the task.

Goal: a GPU path for the exact closures V_D of the split presentation with m ≥ 4 summands. The dense GPU engine (`csd/ic_bounds_big.py`) covers two summands only, and a dense basis does not fit at these sizes (the (5,3) cell at D = 8 has 226,325 columns), so the engine has to exploit sparsity or work out of core. Every speed claim will carry an equality gate against the CPU engines (`csd/ic_bounds_split_m.py` and the Rust `hky2` engine of isogeny-labs/crypto) on the cells both can run.

No code yet; only the `docs/ACTIVE.md` line.

## Test plan

- [ ] equality of dimensions, low-degree profiles and "1 in V_D" with the CPU engines on every shared cell
- [ ] negative control for the equality check
- [ ] measured A/B on a GPU host, with memory figures

prs.title: Root-finding solver for summation systems, and LFD paper update (review fixes, root-finding remark, status)
prs.body_excerpt:
## What this adds

**1. Root-finding solver** for the point-decomposition problem of index calculus on binary curves, without a Gröbner basis.
- `csd/ic_rootfind.py`, `csd/_rootfind.c`: C kernel, `n <= 63`, `m` summands, with enumeration and meet-in-the-middle baselines.
- `rust/ic_rootfind/`: Rust kernel, no dependencies, `n <= 191`, `m = 2, 3`; used for `n = 131`.
- `P_1 + P_2 = T` is a line through `-T`; `x_1 + x_2` and `x_1 x_2` are F_2-affine in the slope, so with `x_i` in a subspace `V` the two-summand step is one linear system in `k + 1` unknowns plus one quadratic. Records: `experiments/ic-rootfind/`.

**2. LFD paper update** (`paper/curve-lfd-bounds.tex`, 49 pp.).

prs.title: Add ctcrypto, a constant-time CNSA 2.0 algorithm library, and the CSfC priorities note
prs.body_excerpt:
Two things:

1. `docs/CSFC_PRIORITIES.md`: a strategy note on where Isogeny Labs fits relative to the NSA CSfC Components List.
2. `ctcrypto/`: a new Rust library (`no_std`, no allocation, no dependencies, no `unsafe`) implementing the CNSA 2.0 algorithms with constant-time handling of secrets.

## ctcrypto

| Module | Algorithm | Checked against |
|---|---|---|
| `mlkem` | ML-KEM-1024 | NIST ACVP 80/80; 300 cases from RustCrypto `ml-kem` |
| `mldsa` | ML-DSA-87 | NIST ACVP full files: 25 keyGen, 90 sigGen, 45 sigVer (committed subset 25/60/45) |
| `aes` | AES-256, AES-256-GCM | NIST ACVP AES-ECB-256 (830 cases + Monte Carlo); Wycheproof AES-256-GCM (66); 220 cases from Python `cryptography` |
| `lms` | LMS/HSS verification | RFC 8554, RFC 9858, NIST ACVP (78), `pyhsslms` (86) |
| `xmss` | XMSS/XMSS^MT verification | 128 signatures from the XMSS reference C code |
| `sha2`, `sha3` | SHA-256/384/512, SHA3, SHAKE | CPython `hashlib` |

`cargo test --release` passes locally and in CI: 66

prs.title: Add the side-channel audit tool (crypto crate, Valgrind) to the toolkit
prs.body_excerpt:
**Re-based on the revised Evidence Lab (2026-11-03, merge `d0e901c`).** Kevin's base revision (`c3f6892`, `fe1c759`, `a59d87b`) replaced experiments with test definitions and added signed evidence, execution modes and classifications. This PR's side-channel tool is now ported onto that model:
- Toolkit runs dispatch to each tool's own runner, in `create_tool_run` and `preflight`.
- The frozen #3296 run is imported through the unsigned results path (`imported_results`, labelled "imported") into its own **"Side-channel audit: crypto crate (demonstration)"** project. Live control runs are added when `ct_dynamic_audit` and Valgrind are connected.
- Static compare pairs are keyed on test definition plus audited target.
- README and SCOPE have been rewritten in the new layout.
